The ECG pattern of ST-segment elevation and ventricular tachycardia after alcohol, in the absence of structural coronary disease, raises the possibility of Brugada syndrome unmasked by alcohol. This is a rare but recognized cause of alcohol-triggered ventricular arrhythmia and represents a more specific subcategory of the current frontier.

The first ECG shows high-grade AV block (node-9), which is a bradyarrhythmia that can be triggered by alcohol. Although ventricular tachycardia is also present, AV block may be the primary alcohol-induced conduction abnormality causing syncope; this refines the frontier toward a specific conduction disorder.
